title: Grammaire : Passé Composé vs Imparfait
description: Comprendre quand utiliser les actions terminées ou les actions d'arrière-plan.
grammarExplanation:
French has two main past tenses: Passé Composé (PC) and Imparfait.

• Passé Composé: Used for specific, completed actions or events. (I ate, I went, I finished)
• Imparfait: Used for internal states, habits, and background descriptions. (I was, I used to, it was raining)

Think of the PC as the 'action' and the Imparfait as the 'scenery'.
- Hier, j'ai mangé (PC) au restaurant. (Specific event)
- Quand j'étais (Imparfait) petit, je mangeais (Imparfait) des fruits. (Habit/Description)

sentences.french: Chaque jour, je mangeais une pomme.
sentences.english: Every day, I used to eat an apple.

sentences.french: Il dormait quand le téléphone a sonné.
sentences.english: He was sleeping when the phone rang.
I was working at the office.

sentences.french: Pierre est arrivé à huit heures.

soudain.explanation: Key word that usually triggers the Passé Composé.

quand.explanation: Often switches between Imparfait (background) and PC (interruption).
